title: Exactness of sheafification on Proj
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its standard grading, and $P=\mathbf P^1_k$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. If $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ is an exact sequence of graded $S$-modules with degree-preserving maps, then the associated sequence of $\mathcal O_P$-modules [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (1) with maps induced by [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial], $0\to\widetilde{M'}\to\widetilde M\to\widetilde{M''}\to0$, is exact.

proof.text: Let $x\in P$ correspond to a homogeneous prime $\mathfrak p$ not containing $S_+$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (1), the three associated sheaves have sections $M'_{(f)},M_{(f)},M''_{(f)}$ on $D_+(f)$. By [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial], each degree-preserving map induces a unique morphism of $\mathcal O_P$-modules, on $D_+(f)$ given by $y/f^m\mapsto\phi(y)/f^m$, and under the stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (c) its map at $x$ is $y/h\mapsto\phi(y)/h$. The functorial composition law in [lem-sc-p1-proj-tilde-functorial] makes the two sheaf maps a complex because the composite graded map is zero.

proof.text: Write $F=\widetilde{M'}$, $G=\widetilde M$, $H=\widetilde{M''}$ with maps $i:F\to G$ and $q:G\to H$. Step 2 gives exactness of $0\to F_x\to G_x\to H_x\to0$ at every $x$. For any open $W$ and $t\in H(W)$, each germ $t_x$ is the image of some germ in $G_x$; by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] represent that germ by a section on a neighbourhood of $x$ and shrink the neighbourhood until its image equals $t$ there. Thus $q$ satisfies the local lifting condition of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (1), hence is surjective. If $s\in G(W)$ and $q_W(s)=0$, exactness at $G_x$ supplies for every $x\in W$ a germ of $F_x$ mapping to $s_x$; represent it by a local section and shrink until its image is $s$ by the equality-of-germs clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting] (2) makes $F\to G\to H$ exact at $G$. Finally apply (2) to $0\to F\xrightarrow{i}G$: if $i_W(s)=0$, then $i_x(s_x)=0$ for every $x\in W$, and stalkwise injectivity gives $s_x=0$; [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] gives a neighbourhood of each $x$ where $s=0$, so the sheaf axiom gives $s=0$ on $W$. This is exactly the local lifting condition for the zero map $0\to F$, and (2) gives exactness at $F$, i.e. injectivity of $i$. Together these are the stated short exact sequence.
